instruction: Ensure all dates in the date column of the spreadsheet follow the YYYY-MM-DD format.

parameters.window_name: New Large Language Models.xlsx - LibreOffice Calc

metadata.explanation: Task requires formatting all dates in the date column to YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., 2023-10-11). The original file has date '2023.9.29' which needs reformatting. Evaluator checks that all dates in column C match the YYYY-MM-DD pattern using regex validation.

llm_judge_reasons: FIXED: Getter now correctly reads cell.number_format (getters/xlsx.py:41) instead of cell values, which properly extracts the date format codes from the spreadsheet cells.
Coverage: Getter checks ALL rows in the date column (range(2, ws.max_row + 1) at line 37), ensuring complete verification of the instruction requirement.

Metric logic: Correctly maps YYYY-MM-DD to various Excel/LibreOffice format code patterns (metrics/xlsx.py:21-29) and uses substring matching to handle format codes with locale prefixes or escaped characters.
Parameter handling: Metric correctly accesses expected.get('format') without the nested 'rules' error pattern, properly handling the type='rule' expected parameter.
Postconfig: Includes Ctrl+S save command to ensure file changes are persisted before verification, addressing state freshness concerns.
Partial scoring: Returns a ratio (matching_count / total) which appropriately handles cases where only some dates are correctly formatted.

Minor concern: The 'contains' check (line 56) could theoretically have false positives, but the acceptable_codes list is specific enough (e.g., 'yyyy-mm-dd', '[$-409]yyyy-mm-dd') to minimize this risk in practice.
